newsitem.title: USA: Big banks report earnings in line with expectations.
newsitem.headline: Big banks report earnings in line with expectations.

text.p: Nationsbank Corp. and other big banks Monday reported higher second-quarter earnings that for the most part came in a shade above expectations on Wall Street.

Nationsbank, the nation's fourth-largest bank, said earnings jumped 26 percent, First Chicago NBD Corp. said its profits rose 5 percent and Bank of New York Co. Inc. reported a 9 percent increase excluding one-time gains. National City Corp., based in Cleveland, also said its earnings rose, up 8 percent.

Nationsbank, based in Charlotte, N.C., said the results reflected a jump in interest income, expense controls and the acquisition of Boatmen's Bancshares Inc. in January, as well as other acquisitions last year.
Net income rose to $762 million, or $1.05 a share, in the quarter, from $605 million, or $1 a share, a year earlier, it said. The results were a penny or two above analysts' forecasts.

"Core revenue growth, stable credit quality and continued expense containment drove this quarter's solid performance," Chief Executive Officer Hugh McColl said, noting the successful integration of St. Louis-based Boatmen's Bancshares.
Interest income jumped 25 percent to $2 billion in the quarter.

First Chicago NBD, the 10th-largest bank, said net income grew to $378 million, or $1.20 a share, in the quarter ended on June 30, from $361 million, or $1.10 a share, a year earlier. The results matched forcasts of $1.20 a share, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates.
The company, based in Chicago, cited lower credit losses and higher interest income for the increase in earnings.

Bank of New York, the No. 17 bank as measured by assets, said earnings rose to $269 million, or 67 cents a share, in the quarter, from $248 million, or 59 cents a share, in the 1996 quarter. The year-ago results exclude a gain of about $31 million on the sale of a credit card portfolio.
Including the gain, net income fell 3 percent. Analysts had forecast earnings of 66 cents a share.

National City, the No. 20, said net income increased to $198.3 million, or 90 cents a share, for the quarter, from $182.8 million, or 82 cents a share, a year earlier. The results came in a penny above average forecasts of 89 cents a share, according to First Call.
"Earnings were driven mainly by fee income growth, excellent credit quality, and control of overhead expense," Chairman David Daberko said in a statement.

Nationsbank stock rose $1.44 to $68.06, First Chicago added $1 to $64 and Bank of New York edged up 25 cents while National City fell 19 cents to $54.69, all in consolidated trading at midday on the New York Stock Exchange.
